{{Quote|I want people to see me. I'm a crime lord. I can't do business if people can't find me.|[[Marn Hierogryph]]|<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic 13">[[Knights of the Old Republic 13|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 13]]</ref>}}
A '''crime lord''' was the local or planetary boss of a criminal organization. Crime lords would often surround themselves with lackeys, [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], or [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] for protection. Crime lords who oversaw smuggling were known as "smuggling czars." "Crime lord" is a gender-neutral term and can be applied to either a male or a female.

The goal of most crime lords was to make money. They would achieve this by participating in any illegal activity that generated income, like extortion, gambling, loan sharking, kidnapping, [[Spice/Legends|spice]] cultivation and distribution, and [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] trading. The [[Squib/Legends|Squib]] [[Slythor]] ran a salvaging ring on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] world of [[Korad]].

Some crime lords preferred to only participate in certain, more "honest" activities such as gambling, loan-sharking, and smuggling because these activities did not harm people as much as extortion or kidnapping. In these activities, the crime lords didn't use cruelty and violence as means of achieving a given goal. Some crime lords even worked with other crime lords to maximize profits.

Most successful crime lords had many police, security, and government officials on their payroll in order to operate efficiently. [[Gangster/Legends|Gangsters]] also regularly entered into the service of crime lords, though usually these goons and thugs working for a crime lord were not paid nearly as well as the crime lord himself.

==Description==
Since crime was virtually impossible to eradicate throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], some beings inevitably rose to the top to take control. Even criminal organizations needed a mastermind behind the scenes to guide  the enterprise. Crime lords were natural leaders, often respected and feared in equal measure for their ruthlessness as leading a criminal organization was not for the weak. Crime lords rose to power in a multitude of ways, often displaying their abilities during their early criminal careers.<ref name="RPG-Core">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook]]''</ref>

During their rise to power, the aspiring crime lord was required to be particularly ruthless,<ref name="RPG-Core" /> and most cultivated a reputation for infamy that inspired fear in their underlings.<ref name="Gamer1">''[[Star Wars Gamer 1]]'' &mdash; Imperial Dispatch: The Crime Lord</ref> Establishing their credentials was a delicate time for them as they either built their own criminal outfit or rose to prominence in an existing one, had their career cut short after a run in with a [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement agency]], or been killed by another crime lord who saw the danger they posed. Some crime lords took control through sheer force and intimidation, others by being expert organizers with a vision. Once on top, crime lords fought a constant battle to remain there. They often found themselves the target of not only ambitious underlings who wanted to usurp them, but also rival crime lords looking to expand their influence. Crime lords would often establish legitimate business fronts as a cover for their illegal activity.<ref name="RPG-Core" />

Crimelords controlled operatives and associates throughout the galaxy. Many individuals supplied them with information from every strata of society. Their information networks ranged from lowly thugs and outlaws, all the way up to politicians, media personalities, and [[Police officer/Legends|law enforcement]] officials. Even experts such as [[Doctor/Legends|doctors]], [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]], and [[Historian/Legends|historians]] could find themselves as contacts within a crimelord's sphere of influence.<ref name="Gamer1" />

Not all crime lords were intent on making profits and being a corrupting influence on society. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], many [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] and [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] became allied with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. They rose through the ranks of the criminal organizations they were affiliated with to take control and then turn their focus to more noble pursuits. These crime lords saw that ridding the galaxy of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], as well as other tyrants and despots, was an important long-term goal. These altruistic crime lords sometimes also suffered from the same problems that more traditional crime lords did. Just because they were attempting to assist others and potentially save the galaxy did not mean that all of those serving under them shared that vision.<ref name="RPG-Core" />

==Hutt crime lords==
[[File:Crime_lord.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] crime lord]]
The [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] were famous for their ruthlessness and success in the underworld. Many Hutts would ransack innocent ships for their cargo. As masters of the criminal underworld, they would steal, cheat, and murder without hesitation, often hiring smugglers such as [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] to transport illegal [[Spice/Legends|spice]], weapons, or slaves. [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorreans]] and [[Weequay/Legends|Weequay]] were commonly employed by Hutts. Hutts tended to ensconce themselves in fortresses, often on remote planets, such as [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba's]] Palace on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. These fortresses were filled with mercenaries, bounty hunters, and innumerable other sycophants. Heading a ruthless criminal organization meant extreme competition and complex intrigues. Hutts that got involved with such activity were often killed or arrested. Only the most cunning, like Jabba and [[Borvo]], stayed at the top of the food chain. Some Hutts, like Jabba, had such an influence that they actually controlled entire planets.

Along with Gamorreans and Weequay, [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] and other ruthless species looking to break into the criminal underworld were common visitors to Hutt palaces. It was well known that no one requested an audience with a Hutt without having something to offer. The Hutts associated with bounty hunters frequently, such as the infamous [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]].

==Behind the scenes==
Crime lord was one the five prestige classes detailed in the [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook|Core Rulebook]] for [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="RPG-Core" />
